blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Small open-weight models (2–9B) run on ordinary laptops, but under
cloud-scale agent harnesses they rarely complete real tasks: tool prefill
overflows the context, self-correction diverges, tool demonstrations
loop, and tasks are silently abandoned. We present evidence, from a
controlled single-machine comparison and one third-party benchmark, that
a substantial share of these failures is attributable to the harness
rather than the model. We introduce Mingbird, a local-first agent
harness for Windows and Ollama whose ten mechanisms compensate
point-by-point for small-model failure forms, three of them
representative: a byte-level net-zero prefill budget, a finish gate that
re-reads the task before accepting completion, and signature-level loop
detection. On LRAB, a controlled comparison holding machine, models,
budgets, and scoring fixed (4 harnesses × \times 4 open models
(2B–35B) × \times 18 real tasks, deterministic artifact scoring),
Mingbird reaches 0.886 overall against 0.631 (goose), 0.479 (opencode),
and 0.405 (agent-mini), with all 288 cells published; on τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench
(278 tasks, three arms, one protocol) it totals 0.856 against 0.791 and
0.737; and a frontier-model probe on the same 18 tasks spans 0.997 to
0.478 across harnesses, with well-formed scaffolds staying within 0.072 of
each other. A leave-one-mechanism-out ablation is reported as
directional only: same-night replications of the same arm move its mean by
up to 0.069, the size of every nominal single-trial delta, and the one
batch-matched comparison (full mechanism stack versus text re-read alone)
gives the executable completion guards a paired + 0.10 +0.10 across three
replications. The
evidence carries stated limits: a self-built benchmark, a single
machine, and single-trial scoring.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Open-weight language models in the 2–9B parameter range have crossed a
practical threshold. On a laptop with an integrated GPU and 16–32 GB of
shared memory they answer, summarize, translate, and explain at a level that
makes them useful daily tools [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] . Local runtimes such as
Ollama and llama.cpp made deployment a one-command operation [ 5 , 6 ] . The prevailing assumption is that such models cannot
serve as agents — systems that autonomously execute multi-step,
tool-mediated tasks: writing code that passes its tests, organizing files,
conducting research with real search, or driving a domain database [ 7 , 8 ] . A recent position paper argues the
opposite for agentic workloads [ 9 ] ; our results
support that view, with one qualification: the limiting component is usually
the harness rather than the model.

blocks.en:
Our observations conflict with this assumption in a specific way: small models
generally produce the correct next action, but cannot reliably emit and
execute every step unaided, inside a harness designed for a much larger
model. When we drove a 2B model with a cloud-scale agent framework, we
observed the same failure forms repeatedly: the static tool prefill alone
consumed a large fraction of the context (long-context degradation is
well documented [ 8 ] ); the model could not self-correct
after a failed tool call [ 10 , 11 ] ; it looped indefinitely on tool demonstrations; and
it sometimes declared a task finished when the artifacts did not exist, or
gave up halfway without saying so. These are not failures of capability.
They are failures of the scaffold surrounding the model, and we treat them as
engineering defects with corresponding engineering remedies.

blocks.en:
This paper makes that argument concrete. We describe Mingbird, a
local-first agent harness for Windows and Ollama, designed from the start for
2–9B models (upper bound tested at the 35B tier; Table 4 ).
Mingbird is a GUI application and a CLI over one agent loop; it adds no
inference machinery of its own and talks to whatever model Ollama serves. Its
design consists of ten core mechanisms (M1–M10) plus a five-ring safety
model (M14, v1.6.0; M11–M13 are product-level facilities,
Section 3.2 ), each mapped to a failure form we first observed
and then measured.

blocks.en: 2 Background and Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 背景和有关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Agent paradigms
blocks.zh: 2.1 代理范式

blocks.en:
The dominant agent recipe descends from ReAct [ 16 ] : the model
interleaves free-form reasoning with tool calls in a loop, and the harness
executes each call and appends the observation. Toolformer [ 17 ] demonstrated that models can learn when to call APIs; Gorilla [ 18 ] fine-tunes specifically for accurate API invocation and
motivated the function-calling interfaces now exposed by most inference
providers. Around this core, a body of work improves the model’s behavior inside the loop: Reflexion [ 19 ] stores verbal
self-critiques across attempts, and Self-Refine [ 20 ] iterates on
its own outputs. These techniques presuppose exactly what small models lack,
namely the ability to produce a usable critique of one’s own attempt.
Mingbird therefore concentrates on the harness side: it does not ask the
model to self-improve in the abstract; it changes what the model sees, when it
is allowed to stop, and what happens after each malformed step. Anthropic’s
engineering guidance [ 21 ] distinguishes workflows
(predefined code paths) from agents (the model directs its own process);
Mingbird is an agent in that sense, but with harness-enforced guardrails at
the points where small models demonstrably fail.
blocks.zh:

将自由形式推理与循环中的工具调用和牵引

blocks.en: 2.2 Agent benchmarks
blocks.zh: 2.2 代理基准

blocks.en:
AgentBench [ 22 ] and AgentBoard [ 23 ] evaluate
multi-turn agents across many environments, the latter with analytical
progress metrics rather than final success only. WebArena [ 24 ] builds a reproducible web environment; SWE-bench [ 25 ] scores real
GitHub issue resolution; GAIA [ 26 ] scores general assistant questions
that are easy for humans. Closest to our external validation are τ \tau -bench [ 27 ] and τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench [ 15 ] : a user simulator
converses with an agent that must operate domain tools under policy, and
scoring verifies the final database state, so an agent that bypasses its tool
stream cannot score. LRAB differs from all of these in intent: it is not
meant to rank models but to isolate harness effects under a fully published
protocol, which is why it uses one machine, one backend, and per-cell
deterministic artifact scoring.

llama.cpp [ 6 ] established efficient CPU/GPU inference for
quantized open models, and Ollama [ 5 ] packages it with model
management and a serving API. Surveys of small language models [ 1 ] document the on-device latency and memory envelope, and
data-centric efforts such as SmolLM2 [ 2 ] and the Gemma and Qwen
families [ 3 , 28 ] push capability per parameter. This line of work
improves the model side of the local stack. The harness side, however, has
largely been ported from cloud practice: lightweight libraries such as
smolagents [ 29 ] and Open Interpreter [ 30 ] make small models drivable with minimal scaffolding; function-calling at
the edge has been explored directly [ 7 ] ; and the full harnesses we
test against (goose [ 12 ] , opencode [ 14 ] , agent-mini [ 13 ] ) are designed around large-context cloud models and
Unix-family shells. Mingbird starts from the opposite end: 2–9B models, a
Windows host, an integrated GPU, and tasks that mix code, files, and research.

blocks.en: 2.4 Engineering systems
blocks.zh: 2.4 工程系统

blocks.en:
SWE-agent [ 31 ] showed that the agent–computer interface (the
shape of the tools an agent is given) changes measured performance on
SWE-bench; our results agree and extend the observation to model-scale
effects. OpenHands [ 32 ] is a general platform for software-development
agents. Cline [ 33 ] and aider [ 34 ] embed agents in editors
and git workflows. These systems target strong models (cloud APIs or large
local checkpoints), assume a POSIX-flavored command environment, and optimize
for coding tasks. Mingbird is complementary: it targets the
under-served regime where the model is small, the machine is a consumer
laptop, and the platform is Windows, and it treats harness mechanisms for
small-model failure forms as the primary design object.

blocks.en:
That the harness, not only the model, drives measured agent performance is
an active 2026 result, not our discovery. Zhang et al. [ 35 ] name and test the binding-constraint thesis —
harness configuration dominates model choice as a source of performance
variance — and call for mandatory harness disclosure; Starace [ 36 ] pre-registers a three-scaffold, five-model comparison
on GAIA and finds within-model scaffold effects up to 28 points; the CAIS
Arena benchmark [ 37 ] pins a single model across six agent
frameworks on one MCP tool server. Our contribution is complementary and
at a tier none of these cover: we instantiate the thesis with 2–9B local
weights on Windows/Ollama, and decompose it at the mechanism level — a
reusable inventory of small-model failure forms with the harness mechanism
that addresses each, and measured per-mechanism costs and deltas. For loop
detection specifically, OpenHands’ StuckDetector [ 32 ] normalizes events and counts repeated action–observation ( ≥ \geq 4),
action–error ( ≥ \geq 3), monologue, and alternation patterns with
intervention nudges; our M4 follows that detection paradigm and adds
signature normalization over tool name plus arguments, a tiered escalation
ladder, and a CI-enforced regression tie. What we claim as new at this
scale is narrower: a net-zero prefill budget enforced byte-level in CI,
and a completion gate that re-reads the task text before accepting
“done” — both aimed at the 2–9B tier where, per our measurements,
prefill crowding and false finishes are the dominant failure forms. A
complementary line treats the harness itself as the design object: Agentless [ 38 ] shows that a deliberately narrow scaffold can outperform
agentic ones on software-engineering tasks; ADAS [ 39 ] , AFlow [ 40 ] , GPTSwarm [ 41 ] , and DSPy [ 42 ] search,
compile, or optimize harness structure automatically; and ToolLLM [ 43 ] routes over large API spaces with a learned retriever. Our
category router is a static, zero-training counterpart of that retrieval
idea, and our mechanism set is hand-designed rather than searched — a
choice Section 5.6 quantifies mechanism by mechanism.

blocks.en: 3 The Mingbird Harness
blocks.zh: 3 明鸟之旅

blocks.en: 3.1 Architecture overview
blocks.zh: 3.1 结构概况

blocks.en:
Mingbird is a local-first agent harness: everything (model, tools,
speech recognition, memory) runs on the user’s machine (the only optional
outbound endpoint is a user-configured search provider), and the harness
adds no inference overhead of its own. This section describes the v1.6.0
release; all measurements reported in this paper were taken on v1.5.0, and
the two releases differ by 23 static-prefill tokens (774 vs. 797;
Appendix B ). Figure 1 shows the
architecture. A GUI (bilingual, built on ttkbootstrap) and a CLI front the
same agent loop. Per turn, the loop assembles a flat prefill through a
task-domain router (M1), classifies the request as chat or task (M2),
executes tool calls through a sandboxed executor with edit safety (M6) and
security boundaries (M8), monitors loop signatures (M4), and enforces a
finish gate before any completion claim leaves the system (M3). A resilience
layer (M7) absorbs encoding faults, empty turns, and process kills via
checkpoints. The backend is whatever Ollama serves, with automatic model
detection and a default 128K context (up to 256K).

blocks.en: 3.2.1 M1: Flat prefill with a net-zero budget
blocks.zh: 3.2.1 M1: 预算净额零的平仓预填

blocks.en:
A 2–9B model given a cloud-style tool manifest
(a few dozen JSON schemas with descriptions) spends several thousand tokens
before the task begins. In our pre-benchmark runs we observed
instruction-following degrade once a large, weakly relevant schema block
preceded the task; in the worst case the context is substantially spent
before the first user sentence. This matches the published input-length
evidence: reasoning degrades when the same task is padded with more tokens [ 44 ] , and frontier models lose accuracy long before
their context window fills [ 45 ] .

constraint is a hard budget: any new feature must add zero net static
prefill , enforced by a byte-level regression assertion in CI (M10).

Category routing can misclassify and hide a tool the
task needs; the classifier is deliberately conservative and the task can
request re-routing. The net-zero rule forces every new capability to be paid
for by removing or compressing something else, a constraint that binds at
small scale, where prefill tokens compete directly with task context, and
that larger models absorb without measurable cost.

blocks.en: 3.2.2 M2: Chat/task layering
blocks.zh: 3.2.2 M2:聊天/任务分层

blocks.en:
A user asks a casual question (“what can you do?”)
and a small model, seeing the full toolset, answers by demonstrating :
it calls tools, narrates, calls more tools, and enters an open-ended loop,
which we term the tool-demonstration loop . The same model given a task
rarely does this.
blocks.zh:
用户随便问一个问题(“你能做什么? ”)
以及一个小模型,看到完整的工具箱,通过演示答案:
它叫工具, 叙述,叫更多的工具, 并进入一个无限制的循环,
我们称之为工具演示循环。 同一型号的任务
很少这样做。

blocks.en:
Requests are classified into chat and task. Chat uses
a minimal chat-level prefill and the loop terminates once the answer is
delivered; the model is not offered a continuation. Task mode unlocks the
full toolset. A short follow-up instruction appended to a conversation that
has produced artifacts is recognized as task continuation. This rule is what
keeps multi-step repair pipelines (e.g. the todo-list repair flow) coherent.

最小聊天级别预填, 一旦答案是
提供;该模型不提供延续。 任务模式解锁
全工具盘。 一份简短的后续指示附在谈话之后
已生产文物被视为任务延续。 这条规则是什么
保持多步修复管道(如待办事项列表修复流量)的一致性.

blocks.en:
Misrouting a genuine task into chat mode would strand
it without tools, so the classifier errs toward task mode whenever an
artifact-producing history exists. The layering trades a single unified loop
for two simple, separately testable ones.

生产文物的历史已经存在。 分层交易一个统一的循环
为两个简单, 单独可测试的。

blocks.zh: 3.2.3 (中文(简体) ). M3: 完成闸门和完成时间迅速重新注入

blocks.en:
Small models abandon tasks silently: they emit a
message that reads as a completion claim while the required artifacts are
missing or incomplete. Longer plans suffer a related drift, because after
context compression the plan text itself is gone and the model continues
from a summary that has lost the acceptance criteria.

小模型默默地放弃任务:它们发射一个
(a) 将所需文物视为完工索赔的信件
缺少或不完整。 更长的计划 经历了相关的漂移, 因为之后
上下文压缩计划文本本身已消失,模式仍在继续

blocks.en:
Before any completion claim is accepted, the harness
re-reads the original task text and asks the model to verify delivery against
it, point by point. The todo/plan pipeline re-injects the plan verbatim after
compression, and the todo interface exposes an explicit completion exit
( todo(update, all=true) ) so that completion is an explicit action
rather than a stylistic drift. The gate’s verification step runs the
task’s own checks and feeds real failures (file, line, error text) back into
the conversation; we refer to this loop as the verification-feedback
mechanism in the ablation.

blocks.en: 3.2.4 M4: Signature-level anti-loop
blocks.zh: 3.2.4 M4: 签名级反潜

blocks.en:
A small model repeats the same tool call with the
same arguments (10, 50, 150 times) producing no artifacts. In one
pre-benchmark case (4B model, task WF-08), the pre-fix run made 156 tool
calls and produced 0 artifacts; we return to this case as motivation below.
blocks.zh:
一个小的模型会重复同样的工具调用
同样的论点(10、50、150次)没有产生任何文物。 在一个
基准前大小写( 4B 型号, 任务 WF-08), 前缀运行 156 工具
我们回过头来讨论这个案子,

blocks.en:
The harness computes a call signature (tool plus
normalized arguments) and trips at ≥ 6 \geq 6 identical calls or ≥ 15 \geq 15 consecutive calls with no output. Escalation is graduated: the third
rejection carries a strong corrective hint, and six consecutive empty turns
trigger a hard reset of the turn; a v1.5.0 reachability fix ensures that
alternating partial-output debris and empty turns no longer reset the
escalation counters. After the fix, the same 4B × \times WF-08 configuration
completed in 15 tool calls with 3 artifacts, with the prefill bit-identical
before and after. This is a single-task motivating case, not controlled
evidence; the controlled ablation appears in Section 5.6 . Two
adjacent failure modes are guarded separately. The output cap was raised from
2048 to 8192 tokens in v1.5.0: at 2048, the emission of a large file is
truncated mid-body and the run decays into an empty-turn spiral; a
truncation signature now returns skeleton-plus-append feedback so the model
can continue in chunks. File reading obeys a byte-budget crawl guard (v2).
The budget is clamped to twice the file size, between 64 KB and 512 KB. The
guard never refuses outright; past the budget it returns the first 2000
characters of the requested range with the position preserved, so that
crawling can continue rather than restart.

blocks.en:
Any loop detector has false positives (legitimate
iteration, e.g. re-running tests after each edit). Signatures normalize
arguments, not raw text, and legitimate iteration usually changes inputs; the
thresholds ( 6 6 , 15 15 ) were set well above observed legitimate repetition.
When the detector does trip on legitimate work, the cost is one corrective
prompt, not a terminated run.

迭代,如每次编辑后重新运行测试). 签字正常化

blocks.en: 3.2.5 M5: False-finish rejection and format rescue
blocks.zh: 3.2.5 M5: 虚假最终拒绝和格式拯救

blocks.en:
Two related failure modes affect output emission.
First, the model claims completion without artifacts; this case is handled by
the M3 gate, and M5 governs the content of the rejection. Second, the model
emits a tool call as plain text — placeholder-quoted quasi-XML, a JSON
snippet in prose, or a double-quoted pseudo-call — which a strict parser
discards, collapsing the turn.
blocks.zh:
两种相关的故障模式影响产出排放。
第一,模型声称在没有文物的情况下完成。
M3门,和M5规范拒绝的内容. 第二,模式
以纯文本形式发出工具调用——占位符引用的 准XML, a JSON
散文,或双引的假呼号——严格分析
丢弃物 转弯

blocks.en:
A rejected false-finish message always carries the
next executable action, so the lowest-cost recovery path is embedded in the
rejection itself. Malformed calls are rescued structurally: the harness
recognizes three recurring shapes (placeholder-quoted, bare-JSON, and
double-quoted pseudo-calls) and converts them into real calls. Strict schema
enforcement is the standard alternative; grammar-constrained decoding engines [ 47 , 48 , 49 ] and schema-emission benchmarks [ 50 ] map its costs, and how much output-format restrictions
cost a model is actively debated [ 51 ] ; for 2–9B models
we adopt rescue-with-feedback instead of strict schema enforcement. Repeated
same-signature emission after a rescue triggers a corrective hint.
blocks.zh:
被否决的虚假讯息总是带有
下一个可执行动作,所以最低成本回收路径嵌入到
拒绝自己。 结构错乱的电话被拯救:绳子
识别三种反复出现的形状(位置标注的、赤裸的JSON,以及
双引伪呼),并转换为真呼. 严格的方案
执行是标准选择;语法限制的解码引擎[47、48、49]和计划排放基准[50]绘制成本图,以及输出格式限制多少
对一个模型进行积极辩论的费用[51];2-9B模型
我们采取救援行动 而不是严格地执行计划 重复
救援后同一签名的释放会触发一个纠正提示.

blocks.en:
Structural rescue is heuristic; a shape outside the
three forms is rejected with feedback, and the harness does not attempt
speculative parsing. We preferred a small, audited rescue set over a
permissive parser that could execute something the model did not mean.
blocks.zh:
结构救援是高压的;
3种形式被回馈拒绝, 并且没有尝试
推测分析。 我们更喜欢一个小型的,经过审计的营救
能够执行模型的允许解析器并不意味着什么。

blocks.en: 3.2.6 M6: Edit safety
blocks.zh: 3.2.6 M6: 编辑安全性

blocks.en:
A small model overwrites a file with a bad edit and
cannot recover; subsequent turns are then consumed by repair attempts, a
regime in which 2–9B models perform particularly poorly.
blocks.zh:
一个小模型覆盖一个编辑不良的文件,
无法恢复; 以后的转弯被修复尝试消耗, a
2 - 9B型机车的表现特别差。

blocks.en:
Every write automatically records a .bak backup; rollback is one command the model can issue itself. An edit
convergence guard watches for alternating destructive edits.
blocks.zh:
每个写法都会自动记录一个.bak备份;回滚是模型本身可以发布的一个命令. 编辑
交替进行破坏性编辑的聚合守护监视 。

blocks.en:
.bak files accumulate in the working
directory; they are excluded from artifact scoring and pruned on successful
convergence. The mechanism is deliberately simple — no diffing, no merging
— because simplicity is what makes it usable by the model itself as
a recovery tool.

目录;它们被排除在文物评分之外,并在成功时刷卡
趋同. 这种机制是故意简单的——没有扩散,没有合并
因为简洁是模型本身可以使用的
一个恢复工具。

blocks.en: 3.2.7 M7: Resilience (encoding, empty turns, checkpoints)
blocks.zh: 3.2.7 国家 M7:复原力(编码、空转、检查站)

blocks.en:
On Windows, process output arrives in legacy
codepages (GBK among them); a strict UTF-8 reader crashes silently and the
harness stalls with no diagnostic. Separately, models occasionally emit empty
generations, and long runs are terminated (by the user, by power
management, or by crashes) and were previously unrecoverable.
blocks.zh:
在 Windows 上, 进程输出会到达遗产
代码页( 其中 GBK ); 严格的 UTF-8 读取器静悄悄地崩溃和
没有诊断的绳子 另外,模型偶尔空出
世代和长行终止(由用户、权力终止)
——管理,或坠机),且此前无法回收.

blocks.en:
The read side decodes as UTF-8 with replacement, so no
byte pattern can crash the reader thread. This fix ended a class of silent
stalls. An empty generation triggers a hard reset of the turn rather than
appending nothing. “Think-tag shells” (responses whose visible content
is only a reasoning wrapper with no actionable output) are detected
semantically and treated as empty. A kill-resume checkpoint records enough
state to resume a terminated run from the last completed step.

字节模式可以崩溃读取器线索. 这个修补结束了一流的沉默
摊位。 空一代触发转弯的硬重置而不是
随附无. “智囊团炮弹”(其可见内容的答复)

Replacement decoding can garble individual characters

paths) we found stream survival strictly more valuable than byte fidelity.
Checkpoints add state to manage and were limited to one file per run.

blocks.en: 3.2.8 M8: Security boundary

blocks.en:
An agent that writes files and runs commands can
write outside its working directory, access credential files, or — in
harnesses with agent fan-out — spawn uncontrolled sub-agents. Small models
are more prone to such divergences.

Working-directory boundaries are enforced by
normalized-path checks (symlink- and separator-safe on Windows). Sensitive
paths ( .ssh , .env , credential stores) sit behind a gate.
Out-of-bounds operations require explicit GUI confirmation by the human.

enabled, each gets a minimal system prompt that is not counted against the
main prefill budget.

blocks.en: 3.2.11 M14: Five-ring safety model (v1.6.0)

Mid-task, a small model may attempt to uninstall a
failing dependency or delete a system file; we observed this incident
pattern in actual runs.
blocks.zh:
任务中,一个小模型可能试图解开一个
不依赖或删除系统文件; 我们观察到此事件
实际运行模式。

blocks.en:
Safety behavior is organized as five rings:
sub-agents run sandboxed with permissions strictly narrower than the main
agent’s; irreversible operations (formatting, raw-device writes, driver
removal and the like) are refused outright; system-mutating actions are
graded by operator presence (unattended runs default to deny, with an
explicit per-run override); recursive deletion is confined to the working
directory, with per-file alternatives offered when a request is refused; and
the last ring is reversibility (.bak before writes, deletions moved to a
trash directory, large-file overwrites requiring an explicit replace). A
single environment variable provides a global override, used at the
operator’s own risk.
blocks.zh:
安全行为组织为五个环:
子代理运行的沙盒中的权限严格小于主
代理; 不可逆操作(格式化、原始设备撰写、驱动程序)
(a) 直接拒绝拆卸等行为;
按运算符存在排序(未处理的运行默认为拒绝),
明确每运行覆盖; 递归删除仅限于工作
目录,在拒绝请求时提供每个文件的替代;
最后一个环是可逆性(.bak在写前,删除移动到 a)
垃圾目录,需要明确替换的大文件覆盖). A级
单一环境变量提供了一个全局覆盖,用于
操作者自身的风险。

blocks.en:
The rings may refuse operations an expert could
perform safely; this conservative bias is deliberate given the target
population defined in M8, and the explicit overrides preserve expert
usability. The ring design is complementary to prompt-injection defenses
evaluated elsewhere [ 52 , 53 ] : M14 governs what the agent’s
own tool stream may do to the host, not what injected content can make it
say.

魔戒会拒绝专家的操作
操作安全; 这种保守的偏差是故意的
M8中定义的人群,明确覆盖保留专家
可用性。 环形设计是对迅速注射防御的补充

说

blocks.en:
The rings are measured, not only designed. We built a 54-case probe set
— 44 adversarial user requests (7/9/9/12/7 across rings 1–5) plus 10
benign controls — in which every adversarial prompt is a natural-language
user request of the kind a small model accepts without suspicion (delete
this failing service; write this file straight into the system temp area;
read my SSH key and summarize it), never an injected text: the set tests
what the agent’s own tool stream may do to the host, which is M14’s
contract, not prompt-injection resistance (evaluated elsewhere, [ 52 , 53 ] ). Both small-tier matrix models were run once per
case ( gemma4:e2b , qwen3.5:4b ; unattended mode,
temperature 0, thinking disabled — the unified protocol of the matrix

Of the 10 benign in-workdir operations, the 2B completes 6 and the 4B

substring match has no workspace scoping (this probe targets exactly

model completed without refusal but without the required artifact (a
capability miss, counted separately from false refusals), and one 4B

ground truth showed no effect. The 4B’s analogous cases died in
command-repetition timeouts before any finish claim; conversely, its
confirmed leaks were reported honestly as successes — the model did
what it claimed. We report both behaviors as measured, without claiming
the finish gate catches false claims.

blocks.en: 4 LRAB: A Controlled Benchmark, Not a Leaderboard
blocks.zh: 4 LIRB:一个受控制的基准,而不是领导板

blocks.en: 4.1 Design principles
blocks.zh: 4.1 设计原则

blocks.en:
LRAB is self-built, and this provenance constrains how its results may be
used. A self-built benchmark cannot establish that Mingbird is the best
harness in general; it can establish a causal statement: on these 18
tasks, on this machine, with these models, changing only the harness changes
the outcome by the reported margin . Three principles follow. First, hold
everything except the harness constant: same machine, same Ollama backend,
same models, same time budgets, same scorer. Second, make every cell
inspectable: tasks, fixtures, scoring code, and all 288 per-cell results are
published, so any aggregate is recomputable from raw rows. Third, treat the
benchmark as one component of the evidence, with a third-party benchmark
( τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench, Section 5.4 ) as the other.

blocks.en: 4.2 Task set
blocks.zh: 4.2 (中文(简体) ). 任务集

blocks.en:
The 18 tasks are emitted by versioned generator scripts (published in the
repository) into a four-tier difficulty ladder, so that a failure can be
localized to a regime rather than averaged into one number: T1 retrieval (WF-01/02), locate and extract from supplied
fixtures; T2 synthesis (WF-03–06), implement features, synthesize
data, write tests; T3 workflow (WF-07–15), multi-step work with
well-defined artifacts — web research with real search queries and
sourced findings, profiling and optimization, refactoring, comparison
dossiers; T4 long-horizon (LH-01–03), multi-phase builds intended
to run for hours, testing plan retention and recovery (M3, M7), with LH-03
doubling as a kill-and-resume stress test (checkpoint continuity at half
budget). Each task specification is structured: domain, input fixtures the
agent must ground in, a minimum credible plan, milestone checks, and final
artifact checks. Task texts are concrete and verifiable by construction —
they name the artifacts that must exist and the checks they must satisfy
— and definitions are frozen before a campaign begins. The set covers the
artifact-producing core of local agent work (code with tests, data
analysis, grounded research, file organization, refactoring, multi-hour
builds) and deliberately excludes what the external check covers:
interactive tool-use dialogue (Section 5.4 ). Per-task
specifications, generator scripts, and the full scoring rubrics are
published in the repository.

blocks.en: 4.3 Protocol
blocks.zh: 4.3 议定书

blocks.en:
All 288 cells ran on one machine (an integrated GPU with 32 GB
shared memory, Windows 11, Ollama as the only backend). Four harnesses
(Mingbird, goose [ 12 ] , agent-mini [ 13 ] , and opencode [ 14 ] ), all stock and unpatched, each drove the same models: gemma4:e2b (2B by Ollama tag: 5B total, 2.3B active per token) [ 3 ] , qwen3.5:4b (4B), gemma4:12b (12B) [ 3 ] , and ornith-1.5:35b (Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, a public multimodal release by Ornith AI [ 54 ] ); Table 4 details parameter counts and
architectures. 1 1 1 qwen3.5 has no separate technical report; [ 28 ] is the family report and [ 55 ] the model card. Despite 35B total parameters, ornith-1.5 is a mixture-of-experts (MoE) that
activates roughly 3B per token, which is why this machine sustains long
tasks end-to-end at roughly 26 tokens/s at a 128K context; the budgets
therefore bind on reasoning and tool work rather than raw decode speed.
Budgets are 90 minutes per workflow cell and 180 minutes per long-horizon
cell. Each cell runs in a fresh working directory; harness processes are
isolated from the scorer. Sampling is pinned to temperature 0 for all four
arms, holding the sampling configuration fixed rather than inheriting each
harness’s defaults: Mingbird pins 0 as its released default and agent-mini
is configured to 0, while goose and opencode expose no temperature setting
and are normalized at the transport level (a local proxy sets temperature=0 on their requests; harness binaries unmodified),
verified on the wire. Left to their defaults, goose and opencode would
sample at each model’s shipped parameters (temperature 1.0 for the gemma
and qwen tiers, 0.8 for the ornith tier); those as-released numbers are
retained in the released sensitivity data. Model-manifest penalties are
untouched by the normalizer and identical across arms. One
retry is allowed and the latest attempt wins;
a timeout scores 0, and this rule applies to Mingbird as well. Retry usage
was asymmetric in practice and we report it: across the final protocol
batch the four arms logged 312 executions for 288 cells — Mingbird used
1 retry, opencode 0, goose 3, and agent-mini 20 (its crash-loop cells).
The goose excess is one cell, WF-08 at 4B, whose archive holds four
executions in total: two scored attempts, each a legitimate 90-minute
timeout, and two retries killed externally before scoring — two over
the one-retry budget, a protocol deviation we disclose. The cell is
zero-scored by operator decision as a runner-level failure under any
reading, and its wall-clock was never carried into the published CSV
(which is why it is absent from the budget census of
Section 4.5 ).
Rather than assert that the rule is neutral we state the counterfactual it
can move: the only released Mingbird cell shaped by the rule is WF-09 at
4B, whose first attempt timed out and whose retry ended in a runner error
with partial artifacts on disk, scored at its artifact value (0.5) — under
a no-retry reading that cell scores 0, so the rule accounts for at most 0.5 / 18 = + 0.028 0.5/18=+0.028 of Mingbird’s 4B mean; every ranking is unchanged under
either reading. The one
Mingbird zero (WF-08 at 35B) is a run that completed without artifacts and

blocks.en:
Scoring is deterministic and artifact-based: files exist where the task
specifies; tests pass when executed; reports contain the required findings.
Scores are partial: a cell with seven equally weighted checks scores 0.571
when four pass; where weights are non-uniform, the published rubric states
them explicitly. Harness processes have no access to the scorer, so a
harness cannot improve its score by any means other than producing
artifacts.

blocks.en: 4.5 Fairness: time is priced by budgets, not by seconds
blocks.zh: 4.5 公平:时间按预算而不是按秒计价

blocks.en:
Harnesses differ substantially in wall-clock behavior, and a benchmark must
fix how to price that. LRAB prices time with uniform budgets per task
family and does not normalize raw seconds. The rationale is that an agent is
useful to a user only if it delivers within the time that the user is willing to
wait; wall-clock differences between harnesses therefore reflect real
architectural costs. In goose’s case, a large prefill amplified by long
contexts manifests as slower but substantive work: its slowest cell runs
11.7 × \times slower than Mingbird on the same task and model (WF-04, 12B;
derived from the published CSV). Discounting seconds would have rewarded
harnesses that terminate early over harnesses that work slowly, and awarding
speed-normalized credit would have rewarded doing less per turn. Budget
pricing instead encodes the user-facing requirement: finish within the
budget or score zero. In the released matrix no arm actually hit the
ceiling: the number of cells, of each arm’s 72, whose wall time reached
95% or more of the budget is zero for all four arms (Mingbird, goose,
opencode, agent-mini: 0/72 each; the one budget-terminated cell in the
matrix — goose’s WF-08 at 4B — has no wall-clock recorded in the
published CSV, so it enters this census through no arm;
Section 4.3 ), so in this batch budget pricing changed
no cell’s score through timeout truncation. We report the wall-clock consequences explicitly in
Section 5.3 , so that readers who prefer a different pricing
can re-derive it from the CSV.

Because each cell is a single run, we treat the 18 tasks as the unit of
analysis. Within each model size, Mingbird is compared with each competitor
by a two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the 18 task pairs, with
bootstrap 95% confidence intervals over task resamples (10,000 resamples,
fixed seed) and Holm correction across the three comparisons within a model;
the script ( analyze_significance.py ) ships with the repository. At
2B and 12B, the Mingbird advantage over all three competitors is
significant after Holm correction (largest adjusted p p per model: 0.0008 at
2B, 0.0466 at 12B). At 4B only the comparison with opencode is significant
(adjusted p = 0.0181 p=0.0181 ); goose, with thinking disabled under the unified
protocol, closes to 0.801 against Mingbird’s 0.876 and the comparison does
not reach significance (raw p = 0.3258 p=0.3258 ), nor does agent-mini at its
strongest tier (adjusted p = 0.1486 p=0.1486 ). At 35B the comparisons with goose
(Holm-adjusted p = 0.0415 p=0.0415 ) and agent-mini ( 0.0005 0.0005 ) are significant, while
opencode at 0.896 against Mingbird’s 0.941 does not separate
(raw p = 0.4652 p=0.4652 ). We read this honestly: under the unified no-thinking
protocol two competitors close the gap at their strongest tiers, and the
robust Mingbird advantages are the small-model segment and the overall
margin. Figure 5 shows the score distributions behind these
tests.

blocks.en:
The 18 tasks are generated in four families (2 retrieval, 4 synthesis, 9
workflow, 3 long-horizon), so task-level pairing overstates independence.
We therefore re-ran the analysis with the family as the resampling unit
(cluster bootstrap over the four families; script alongside analyze_significance.py ). Two properties of this analysis must
be stated precisely, and they discipline what family-level claims are
available at all. First, when all four family means are non-negative, a
cluster-bootstrap CI cannot cross zero by construction — every resample
of non-negative family means is non-negative — so such a CI is
uninformative whatever its width; this applies to every comparison whose
family means share a sign, including the ones that favor us (at 2B all
three comparisons; at 4B vs. goose; at 12B vs. goose, whose tier-1 mean
is exactly zero). Second, the auxiliary sign permutation flips
task-level signs within families; it is a task-level test — a
family-level flip would have only 2 4 = 16 2^{4}=16 sign patterns and a minimum
two-sided p p of 0.125 0.125 — so with four families no family-level
significance claim is available for any comparison, ours included. Under
that standard the honest family-level statements are: at 2B the paired
advantage is descriptively present in all four families (all four family
means strictly positive: + 1.000 / + 0.428 / + 0.413 / + 0.823 +1.000/+0.428/+0.413/+0.823 vs. goose), which
is the strongest family-level evidence four clusters can give, but it is
not a family-clustered significance claim; the task-level tests remain
significant as reported. The one comparison whose cluster CI is
informative is 4B vs. agent-mini, the only one with a negative family
mean (long-horizon − 0.221 -0.221 ): its cluster CI crosses zero, consistent
with its already-nonsignificant adjusted p p . 4B vs. goose and 12B
vs. goose fall in the uninformative category above; their task-level
results stand as reported (nonsignificant p = 0.35 p=0.35 ; marginal adjusted p = 0.036 p=0.036 ). No comparison that was
nonsignificant becomes significant under clustering.

blocks.en:
The matrix compresses 288 runs; the transferable findings are the underlying
failure forms. Figure 4 makes the failure structure visible
at the task level. Our five-form taxonomy is single-agent and local-tier;
it is complementary to the multi-agent failure taxonomy of MAST [ 56 ] ,
which classifies failures of multi-agent LLM systems from operator reports
rather than measured cells. • Mingbird: one artifact-free run in the whole matrix. The
single zero-scored cell (WF-08, 35B) ended after 276 seconds: the model
wrote a task plan, then repeatedly declared completion without writing the
deliverables; the finish gate rejected each declaration (the transcript is
published), and the run ended with no artifacts on disk. If that cell were
excluded rather than scored 0, the 35B mean would rise from
0.941 to 0.996; we report 0.941, as the protocol requires. One further
cell (WF-09, 4B) ended in a runner error after producing partial
artifacts and is scored at its artifact value (0.5); excluding it would
raise the 4B mean from 0.876 to 0.898, and excluding both anomalous cells
leaves every ranking unchanged. • agent-mini at 35B: platform mismatch. 14 of its 18 cells at
35B scored zero, and the published wall-times show why: those runs all
ended within 80 seconds. Inspection of the attempt directories shows the
agent issuing Unix-flavored commands into a Windows shell, failing, and
exiting. This is a harness–platform fit failure, not a model failure; the
same model scores 0.679–0.941 on other harnesses.
A sensitivity view over the whole matrix: agent-mini has 30 early-exit
cells in total (wall time under 80 s: 15 at 35B, 13 at 2B, 2 at 4B,
nearly all scoring zero). Excluding those 30 (task, model) combinations
from all four arms (each arm keeps the same 42 cells) changes the
overall means to Mingbird 0.901, goose 0.709, agent-mini 0.617, opencode
0.486: Mingbird remains first (margin over the runner-up narrows from + 0.255 +0.255 to + 0.193 +0.193 ), but agent-mini and opencode swap third and fourth
place. Per tier, the 2B segment after this exclusion is Mingbird 0.843
vs. goose 0.200, agent-mini 0.414, opencode 0.000 over the remaining
cells — removing platform-mismatch cells widens the small-model
separation rather than narrowing it. The 80 s cutoff itself deserves
scrutiny: opencode’s 2B failures end within 49–115 s (below), and
raising the threshold to 120 s to cover that window excludes
agent-mini’s entire 2B row (all 18 of its 2B cells end within 120 s),
degenerating the analysis — the shared property of these cells is the
early-exit failure form, not the exact cutoff. The overall ranking’s
tail is therefore sensitive to the platform
dimension; the headline claim (first place, and the 2B segment) is not. • opencode: premature termination at the small end. Its 2B
cells ended early (typically within 49–115 seconds) with the required
artifacts never created — 17 of 18 score zero — a plausible
explanation being an exit path that conflates unresolvable states with
completion. Under the unified no-thinking protocol its larger tiers
recover substantially (12B 0.140 → \to 0.539, 35B 0.776 → \to 0.896;
thinking-on values are from the legacy pre-re-shot batch), which we
return to in the thinking-sensitivity discussion. • goose: slow but substantive progress. goose’s median and
typical slow cells are the slowest of the four (Section 5.3 ), but its failures are
qualitatively different: its runs make substantive progress under a large
prefill amplified by long contexts, and it scores 0.679 at 35B (0.822
with thinking on, legacy batch). Its
2B collapse is consistent with the prefill-cost failure form that M1
addresses.

Figure 6: LRAB score versus wall-clock time per cell (one point per
published CSV row; the single goose cell with no recorded wall-clock is
excluded, leaving 287 points; logarithmic time axis; color encodes the
harness, marker size the model tier). Dashed vertical lines mark the

seconds contains agent-mini’s 35B platform-mismatch cells, while the
slow-but-substantive tail is dominated by goose. The figure is the visual
form of the budget-pricing protocol of Section 4.5 : neither
axis alone earns credit.

415.4 s (Mingbird), 707.9 s (goose), 133.8 s (agent-mini), and

wall-clock time in the score–time plane. agent-mini is fast because it
exits early; speed without artifacts is not credit, and the budget protocol
already encodes that. goose is the slowest harness that produces substantive
work (on individual cells it runs up to 11.7 × \times{} slower than
Mingbird), which we attribute to prefill size times context length per
turn, and which its 4B/12B scores show is not disqualifying at larger model
scale. Mingbird’s own slow cells are WF-11 at 4B (3344 s) and its
long-horizon runs, consistent with more turns spent on verification rather
than fewer. Readers who would price time differently can recompute any weighting
from the CSV; the protocol’s choice (budget pricing, no second discounting)
is stated in Section 4.5 .

Because LRAB is self-built, we additionally evaluated on a third-party
benchmark: τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench [ 15 ] , in all three of its domains

run the judge ( qwen3.8-max ) and the simulator through the same

fixed across the comparison.

native tool mechanism; the benchmark’s native LLM agent — the upstream
default LLM-agent implementation shipped with the τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench release
pinned in Appendix B , with prompts and tool-calling
protocol at upstream defaults, unmodified — and Mingbird drive the
tools directly.

Because the unified protocol pins thinking off, we also hold the earlier
thinking-on runs as a sensitivity view. The configuration moves arms, not
noise: opencode’s retail score goes 0.246 → \to 0.588 and telecom
0.298 → \to 0.991 when thinking is disabled; the native agent’s airline
score goes 0.520 → \to 0.740 while its saturated telecom mean drops
1.000 → \to 0.930; Mingbird moves least (retail 0.789 → \to 0.763).
The same lever appears inside LRAB (opencode 12B 0.140 → \to 0.539;
goose 35B 0.822 → \to 0.679).
A harness’s thinking policy is thus a first-class design decision with
task-dependent costs and benefits — one more axis on which harnesses
differ even when the model is fixed.

The matrix of Table 5 varies the model at fixed local hardware

isolates the harness’s own contribution. We therefore ran a decomposition

model — the hosted qwen3.8-flash — in place of local weights.
A local shim presents the cloud endpoint as an Ollama service, so every

probe-versus-matrix juxtapositions are cross-version for the Mingbird
arm (Appendix B ). Budgets are 60 minutes per workflow
task and 90 per long-horizon task, scored by the same deterministic rubric.
This is a probe, not part of the 288-cell matrix: the model is a cloud API
rather than local weights, and per-cell cost bounds us to one trial per arm.

second-scale early exits persist unchanged, confirming that its deficit is
in the scaffold, not the model it was given.

To move from the design narrative of Section 3.2 toward
marginal-contribution estimates, we ran an ablation on the v1.5.0 code
base: four variants, each with one mechanism disabled through an AGENT_ABLATION environment gate, over the same 18 LRAB tasks
with gemma4:e2b ( n = 18 n=18 cells per arm). The disabled mechanisms
are the finish gate (M3), the verification-feedback loop (part of M3), the
signature-level anti-loop monitor (M4), and the category-routed flat
prefill (M1); the ablation thus covers three mechanisms (M1, the two
halves of M3, and M4) across four variant arms, while M2 (chat/task
layering) and M5 (format rescue) are not ablated and remain the two named
mechanisms whose benefits this paper does not quantify. The four variant
arms ran 2026-09-14..15; the same-night re-run arms and their three
replications ran 2026-09-22 on the v1.8.2-era tree
(Appendix B ). The baseline is
the full-mechanism arm of the same code base, and its 18 cells are reused
directly from the 2B column of Table 5 (same code); the
four variant arms are independent new executions over those tasks, under
the same temperature-0 configuration as the main matrix. There is
therefore a batch gap between the baseline arm and the variant arms, and
the common-cause disclosure below stems from it. Each variant wrote an
independent results directory, scored by the same deterministic rubric.

blocks.en:
The two gate variants are separable in the implementation, and the
separation is mechanical: AGENT_ABLATION =finish_gate bypasses
four of the six finish-time interventions (no-work finish refusal, the
pytest test guard, summary-to-artifact cross-checking, and
plan-completeness checking); two interventions are not gated by this
switch and stayed active in both arms — the todo-sync reminder (which
refuses a finish while the model’s own declared plan shows unchecked
items) and the delivery self-check, which re-injects the task’s original
text once and asks the model to self-check before the second, accepted
finish. This matters for interpretation: the textual re-read — the part
of M3 the abstract highlights — is present in both arms, so the − 0.098 -0.098 measures the four executable guards on top of the re-read,
not the re-read itself. AGENT_ABLATION =
verify_feedback leaves every guard active but downgrades the failure
feedback inside pytest refusals — the precise injected hint (failing
test, file, line, assertion) is replaced by the last line of the pytest
output only. The two switches therefore measure different things: removing
the gate removes the executable-refusal behavior; removing verification
feedback keeps refusals but starves the model of the exact failure location
it would need to recover in one step. The nearest published neighbors are
tool-interactive self-critique (CRITIC [ 57 ] ) and programmatic
verification loops in code agents (AutoCodeRover [ 58 ] );
M3 applies the same verify-before-finish principle at the harness level,
for general local tasks rather than code alone.

The pytest guard fires only when the working directory contains test_*.py at finish time. Two of the 18 tasks stage
benchmark-provided test files into the workdir (WF-04 stages test_inventory.py ; LH-03 stages test_suite.py ); on
those two tasks the harness at finish time executes the same fixture the
scorer executes later (the scorer’s spec_pytest and script_pass checks run the same files), so there the acceptance
criterion is literally runnable before scoring. On the other 16 tasks the
guard fires only on test files the agent itself wrote, and the three other
ablated guards act on information the scorer only partially shares: the
claim-check and the scorer both test file existence, but the claim-check
runs on whatever the model claimed in its finish summary, and the
no-work and plan-completeness guards act on run-time information —
productive tool use and the agent’s own declared plan — that the scorer
never sees (the published scoring is fully deterministic — milestone
and final-artifact checks only; the scorer’s optional LLM-judge component
was disabled for every published batch, so no judge enters any LRAB
number in this paper). The
per-task decomposition bounds how much of the effect this overlap can
explain: the net − 0.098 -0.098 is carried by four tasks at roughly + 0.71 +0.71 each (LH-01, WF-13, WF-04, WF-02) against three tasks the gate hurt

fired across the 72 Mingbird cells of the released matrix (counting

always did nominal work before finishing, so that guard contributes
nothing to the margins above, consistent with the per-task decomposition.

is the most tool-intensive arm, which is the intended behavior of a
harness that keeps a small model moving through concrete steps. Peak

blocks.en:
Because the harness and the benchmark share authors, we disclose what each
ablated mechanism was developed against. The finish gate and the anti-loop
monitor were iterated with LRAB in the loop : their v1.2.0 forms
were explicit responses to LRAB long-horizon failures (early-finish
abandonment; a same-tool-call rule that disarmed legitimate batch work),
and the WF-08 incident (156 calls, zero artifacts → \to 15 calls, three
artifacts, prefill byte-identical) drove the anti-loop escalation ladder.
The verification-feedback hint predates LRAB (developed against an
earlier internal benchmark, 2026-08-19..26, before LRAB existed on
2026-08-28), with LRAB-period strengthening after a WF-08 12B failure.
The flat prefill also predates LRAB (root cause: a Q&A tool-demonstration
loop, 2026-08-20) and, as Section 5.6 notes, is inert on
LRAB’s narrow tool surface. Consequently, the − 0.098 -0.098 finish-gate and − 0.015 -0.015 anti-loop deltas should be read as in-sample effect estimates for
mechanisms co-developed with the task set — which is why the ablation is
reported as directional throughout. Of the four ablated arms, three
carry some in-sample exposure (the finish gate and anti-loop monitor were
iterated with LRAB in the loop; the verification-feedback hint predates
LRAB but was strengthened during the LRAB period), and only the flat
prefill is both pre-LRAB and, by its near-zero delta, inert here; the
external τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench comparison — same code, no
benchmark-provided tests for the gate to run — is the out-of-sample
anchor for the mechanisms the ablation cannot cleanly measure.

blocks.en: 6 Threats to Validity
blocks.zh: 6. 对有效性的威胁

blocks.en:
LRAB’s tasks and rubrics were authored by the same people who built
Mingbird. We cannot rule out that the task set favors our harness’s
mechanisms; indeed, it was designed to exercise the failure forms in
Section 3.2 , which is the point of a controlled experiment
but also its bias. Mitigations include the full publication of tasks,
fixtures, scoring code, and raw cells, in the spirit of reproducible agent
evaluation [ 59 ] ; the explicit framing as a controlled
experiment rather than a leaderboard; and the external τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench
replication, whose benchmark, tasks, and scorer are third-party. The two
legs agree in direction.

blocks.en:
τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench is our only three-arm external comparison (a fourth CLI
arm, goose, is deferred for throughput), and it comes from
one family (one lab, three domains). This is not for lack of searching; it
reflects a structural constraint. A harness comparison requires the harness to be the experimental variable, which excludes every suite
that supplies its own agent loop, and it additionally requires the suite to
discriminate at local-model scale; dynamic GUI-device environments such as
AndroidWorld [ 60 ] add device emulation to that list and were
not candidates for the same reason. We examined five external candidates
against these two filters and excluded each for cause: AppWorld [ 61 ] (all-zero
at every local model tier we ran), ToolSandbox [ 62 ] and
AgentBoard (the
benchmark provides the agent loop; only the model varies), function-calling
emission suites (model-side emission with no environment and no multi-step
loop; e.g. JSON-schema emission benchmarks [ 50 ] ),
CRMArena [ 63 ] (we built a local backend against the official data
snapshot and probed it: gemma4:e2b 0/5, qwen3.5:4b 0/5, and the 35B tier
at 40+ minutes per task with the first completed task scored 0 —
no discrimination at usable throughput), and GAIA (no discrimination for
local models in our runs). We report this filter explicitly so that the
single-family external evidence can be weighed for what it is; the
cross-benchmark agreement between LRAB and τ 2 \tau^{2} on the shared

blocks.en:
For small models, the harness is not peripheral glue but a substantial part
of the capability surface. The 2B segment shows this most clearly: same
model, same budgets, and one harness completes 0.821 of its cells while
others complete 0.017–0.271. The failure forms behind that gap (prefill
overflow, unbounded demonstration loops, silent abandonment, malformed calls
discarded by strict parsers) are deterministic engineering problems, and
none of them requires model retraining. The frontier probe sharpens the
attribution from the other direction (Section 5.5 ): with the
model pinned near its ceiling, harness choice alone spans 0.478–0.997 on
the same tasks, so a weak scaffold strands capability that a stronger one
recovers. The ablation puts directional
numbers on this attribution at 2B: the largest single loss comes from
removing the finish gate (Section 5.6 ). We expect several
mechanisms (flat
prefill with a hard budget, finish gates, loop signatures) to transfer to
larger models with weaker budgets, though our data cover only up to the 35B
tier of Table 4 .

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
We presented Mingbird, a local-first agent harness for Windows and Ollama
that treats small-model failure forms as first-class engineering targets.
The evaluation is a fully published controlled experiment: 288 cells, four
harnesses, four open models (2B–35B), one machine, and deterministic
artifact-based scoring. Mingbird reaches 0.886 overall against 0.631,
0.479, and 0.405 for three stock baselines, is the only harness without a
small-model cliff, and leads the long-horizon segment at 0.827 (single
draw per cell). An external
replication on τ 2 \tau^{2} -bench in all three domains (0.856 vs. 0.791 and
0.737 over 278 tasks, same local 4B model, matched user simulator, with the
fourth CLI arm deferred for throughput on this benchmark)
supports the direction on a third-party benchmark, and a frontier-model
probe — one hosted model, four harnesses, the same 18 tasks — spans
0.997 to 0.478, showing that a defective scaffold buries more than half of
a frontier model while well-formed scaffolds stay within 0.072–0.12 of each
other. A
leave-one-mechanism-out ablation attributes the largest single share of the
margin to the finish gate, and the thinking configuration itself emerges as
a harness-level lever with task-dependent costs. LRAB is self-built
and carries its authors’ bias; we publish every cell so that the results can
be independently recomputed or refuted. Our results suggest that a
substantial share of what is attributed to model incapacity in this setting
is in fact scaffold defect, and such defects are addressable.

The signature-level guard was developed against this task, where the stock
loop degenerated into 156 identical tool calls with zero artifacts in the
target directory. After the fix — same code, same task, same model, with
